rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Not named in the Qur'an — rests on the general permission of trade (2:275) and mutual consent (4:29).
rows.detail_long: Murabaha has no dedicated verse. Its legitimacy hangs on 'Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba' (2:275) and the mutual-consent rule of 4:29 — the same two verses every later cost-plus structure cites.

hadith_meta.narrator: abu Hamzah, from Imam al-Baqir (abu Ja'far)
topics_app: Selling for Capital with an Additional Certain Percentage Profit (Murabahah)

rows.detail: Murabahah chapter. Imam al-Baqir: no murabaha resale until each item's cost basis is made clear — the disclosure rule stated by name.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: a man buys goods in bulk, prices each piece to cover capital, then wants to sell 'in the form of Murabahah (capital plus a certain percent profit)'. The Imam: 'No, he cannot do so until he makes it clear that the item has a fixed price.' The cost-transparency core of murabaha, in a chapter titled for it.

rows.name: Man la yahduruh al-Faqih vol.3, al-Saduq

hadith_meta.narrator: Maysir the fabric seller, from Imam al-Sadiq (Abu Abdullah)

rows.detail: Murabaha on credit. Imam al-Sadiq: goods bought on credit and resold as murabaha carry the same credit period to the buyer — cost disclosure includes the terms.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: the fabric-seller buys merchandise on credit, states its valuation, sells at profit. The Imam rules: 'If you sell it on a profit basis (Murabaha), then he is entitled to the same credit period as you.' Murabaha's honesty duty covers not just price but how it was financed.

rows.name: Ibn Abbas (attrib., Tanwir al-Miqbas)
rows.detail: The earliest attributed gloss on 2:275: deferred-sale increase is permitted trade; increase on a due debt is the forbidden riba.
rows.detail_long: Tanwir al-Miqbas (in the app) on 2:275 reads the deniers' claim 'trade is just like usury' as equating increase at the START of a deferred sale with increase when the term FALLS DUE — and the verse's answer: Allah permits the former (trading) and forbids the latter (usury). The exact line every cost-plus (murabaha) structure stands on. Attribution to Ibn Abbas is traditional, not critical — hence 'attrib.'
rows.evidence_display: Tanwir al-Miqbas (attrib. Ibn Abbas), on Q2:275 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app file en-tafsir-ibn-abbas/surah-002.json (batch1_source_extract2.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: al-Tabari
rows.detail: Al-Tabari's commentary on 2:275 fixes the trade-versus-riba distinction murabaha rests on.
rows.detail_long: Al-Tabari's 2:275 treatment (12,000+ chars in the app file) opens with the philology of riba — 'increase upon a thing' — and the pre-Islamic practice of doubling a debt for extra term, then draws the line: profit from sale is permitted trade, increase on a debt for time is the forbidden riba. The distinction every murabaha manual rests on.
rows.evidence_display: Jami' al-Bayan (Tafsir al-Tabari), on Q2:275 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim this session from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract.json)

rows.name: al-Qurtubi
rows.detail: Al-Qurtubi develops the same trade/riba reading of 2:275 with the Maliki legal detail.
rows.detail_long: Al-Qurtubi's 2:275 commentary (23,800+ chars in the app file) works the trade/riba boundary into Maliki rulings on valid sale forms — the ahkam frame later cost-plus manuals cite.
rows.evidence_display: al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an, on Q2:275 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim this session from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract.json)

rows.name: Ibn Kathir
rows.detail: Ibn Kathir on 2:275: the trade/riba divide as the frontier between lawful acquisition and 'illegally acquiring people's money'.
rows.detail_long: The app's Ibn Kathir passage on 2:275 (read this session) frames riba-eaters as those who 'illegally acquire people's money, using various evil methods and wicked ways', against the permitted path of trade — the moral casing around the verse murabaha relies on.
rows.evidence_display: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, on Q2:275 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim from app file en-tafisr-ibn-kathir/surah-002.json (batch1_source_extract2.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani
rows.detail: Ma'ariful Qur'an on 4:29: the protection of property and the consent rule as the gate every sale — murabaha included — must pass.
rows.detail_long: The app's Ma'ariful Qur'an passage on 4:29 (read this session) sets the verse in its Surah al-Nisa' sequence: guarding rights and property, then forbidding wrongful consumption of wealth — with trade by mutual consent as the lawful channel. rows.timeline_year_basis: app core.json dod (F0778); Muwatta = earliest surviving school literature
rows.name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
rows.detail: Al-Muwatta. The earliest juristic murabaha text in the app corpus: Malik rules which costs may enter the murabaha base and which may not.
rows.detail_long: Muwatta 1425 read verbatim: transporting goods enters the cost base; the trader's own labour, ironing, folding, house rent do not — unless disclosed to and accepted by the buyer. Bleaching, tailoring, dyeing count like the goods. Undisclosed items void the profit claim; if the goods are gone, transport is reimbursed without profit; if not gone, the sale is void unless renegotiated. Murabaha arrives in law fully formed as a DISCLOSURE doctrine. CONTEXT: no Sunni prophetic hadith names murabaha — the contract enters the tradition through juristic literature; this Muwatta chapter is that entry point.
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app file muwatta-malik.json (batch1_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: al-Shafi'i
rows.detail: Al-Shafi'i's Kitab al-Umm holds the seminal passage: a lawful cost-plus resale — the trust-sale foundation of bank murabaha.
rows.detail_long: The al-Umm passage ('buy this and I will give you a profit — this deal is lawful') is the text Sami Hamoud later builds three-party bank murabaha on. App holds the work as F0776-B51.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.2; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: al-Kasani
rows.detail: Al-Kasani gives the standard definition: sale at the first price plus a disclosed excess as profit.
rows.detail_long: Bada'i al-Sana'i defines murabaha precisely — resale at cost plus declared markup — the definition modern standards still quote. Finance-local figure; death 587 AH / 1191 CE from standard references.

rows.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
rows.detail: Ibn Qudama treats murabaha among the named trust-sales for the Hanbalis; Malikis and Hanafis do likewise.
rows.detail_long: Al-Mughni files murabaha with tawliya and wadi'a as buyu' al-amanah (trust sales) — valid when cost is truthfully disclosed. App book F0749-B50.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.2; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: Sami Hassan Hamoud
rows.detail: Sami Hamoud engineers 'Murabaha to the Purchase Orderer' in his Cairo PhD — the bank three-party structure.
rows.detail_long: His thesis Tatwir al-A'mal al-Masrifiyya grounds bank murabaha on al-Shafi'i's al-Umm passage and recommends it to the Islamic Development Bank and Dubai Islamic Bank — the single most consequential piece of modern financial ijtihad.
rows.evidence_display: Sami Hamoud engineers 'Murabaha to the Purchase Orderer' in his Cairo PhD

rows.name: Jordan Islamic Bank
rows.detail: Hamoud's model applied in practice at Jordan Islamic Bank (1978-79).
rows.detail_long: The first live deployment of murabaha-to-the-purchase-orderer as a mainstream bank product.

rows.name: OIC Fiqh Academy
rows.detail: OIC Resolutions 40-41 make the customer's promise binding — the legal key to bank murabaha.
rows.detail_long: The 5th-session resolutions settle that a unilateral promise to purchase can be made binding, closing the gap that made three-party murabaha legally fragile.
rows.evidence_display: OIC Resolutions 40-41 make the customer's promise binding

rows.name: OIC Fiqh Academy
rows.detail: OIC Fiqh Academy declares organized tawarruq (reverse murabaha) impermissible.
rows.detail_long: Organized tawarruq — murabaha chains engineered purely to generate cash — is ruled a hiyal (legal artifice) defeating the contract's purpose.

rows.timeline_year_basis: adopted as Shari'ah *rules* 29-31 May 2000 (meeting 4); readopted as a Standard at meeting 8, 11-16 May 2002
rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 8 codifies murabaha for the industry.
rows.detail_long: SS8 sets the documentation, sequence-of-ownership and promise rules for murabaha and murabaha-to-the-purchase-orderer. VERIFIED adoption: rules adopted 31 May 2000, reformatted as Standard 16 May 2002. CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT THIS SESSION (ss1.txt): 3/1/1 — the Institution shall not sell any item in a murabaha transaction before it acquires it (ownership-before-sale); 4/1 — no commitment fee may be taken from the customer; 4/3 — contract-document expenses borne evenly by both parties.
rows.internal_ref: Adoption page verified earlier session; clauses 3/1/1, 4/1, 4/3 read verbatim from ss1.txt this session (2026-07-14)

rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: Murabaha dominates bank financing — 80-90% of some banks' operations, >55% GCC average (2016) — and is the most criticized structure.
rows.detail_long: Estimates put murabaha at over half of all Islamic financing. Abdullah Saeed (finance scholars S028) and others criticize it as economically replicating interest; defenders answer that ownership risk and asset-backing distinguish it.
